ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $BE\perp AC$ at point D, and $AD = CD$, $BD = ED$. If $\angle E = 35^\circ$, what is the value of $\angle ABC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $BE\perp AC$ and $AD=DC$,\\
it follows that $BA=BC$,\\
which implies $\angle ABD=\angle CBD=\frac{1}{2}\angle ABC$,\\
Considering $\triangle ADB$ and $\triangle CDE$, we have\\
\[
\begin{cases}
AD=DC\\
\angle ADB=\angle EDC\\
BD=DE
\end{cases},
\]
hence, $\triangle ADB\cong \triangle CDE$,\\
which means $\angle E=\angle ABD=35^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle ABC=2\angle ABD=\boxed{70^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: Use coordinates/trigonometry. From the image, treat D as the intersection of AC and BE, with A and C on one line and B and E on the perpendicular line. From the text, set D=(0,0), put AC on the x-axis and BE on the y-axis. Let A=(-a,0), C=(a,0), B=(0,-b), E=(0,b), because AD=CD and BD=ED. The given angle E is angle BEC, between the downward vertical vector EB and vector EC=(a,-b); call it θ=35°. Its tangent is a/b. method.CoT_raw:

推理：按照坐标/三角方法，令 D=(0,0)，把 AC 放在 x 轴上，把 BE 放在 y 轴上。由 AD=CD、BD=ED，可设 A=(-a,0)，C=(a,0)，B=(0,-b)，E=(0,b)，其中 a,b>0。

已知 \angle E=\angle BEC=35^\circ。向量 EB=(0,-2b)，方向竖直向下；向量 EC=(a,-b)。所以角 BEC 与竖直向下方向之间的水平偏移为 a、竖直偏移为 b，因此 tan\angle BEC=a/b。

在点 B，BD 竖直向上，BA=(-a,b)。角 ABD 与竖直向上方向之间同样有水平偏移 a、竖直偏移 b，因此 tan\angle ABD=a/b。由于这两个角都是锐角，所以 \angle ABD=\angle BEC=35^\circ。

又因为 A=(-a,0)、C=(a,0) 关于 y 轴对称，BA 和 BC 关于 BD 对称，所以 \angle ABD=\angle DBC。因此 \angle ABC=2\angle ABD=2\times35^\circ=70^\circ。

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $BE\perp AC$ at point D, and $AD = CD$, $BD = ED$. If $\angle E = 35^\circ$, what is the value of $\angle ABC$?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $BE\perp AC$ and $AD=DC$,\\
it follows that $BA=BC$,\\
which implies $\angle ABD=\angle CBD=\frac{1}{2}\angle ABC$,\\
Considering $\triangle ADB$ and $\triangle CDE$, we have\\
\[
\begin{cases}
AD=DC\\
\angle ADB=\angle EDC\\
BD=DE
\end{cases}
\]
hence, $\triangle ADB\cong \triangle CDE$,\\
which means $\angle E=\angle ABD=35^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle ABC=2\angle ABD=\boxed{70^\circ}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure, there are two line segments AC and BE intersecting at point D; A is located at the upper left, C is located at the lower right, B is located at the lower left, and E is located at the upper right; the figure also connects BA, BC, and CE. ∠E is the angle at point E formed by EB and EC, and ∠ABC is the angle at point B formed by BA and BC.

Then reason: From the problem statement, BE ⟂ AC at D, and AD = CD, BD = ED, so D is the midpoint of AC and BE. When rotating 180° about D, A will correspond to C, and B will correspond to E, so ∠ABD corresponds to ∠CED. Because D is on BE, ∠CED is exactly the angle at point E, namely ∠E = 35°, so ∠ABD = 35°. Also because BD is on BE, and BE ⟂ AC, and AD = CD, BD is the perpendicular bisector of AC. Reflection about BD will map A to C, so BD bisects ∠ABC, namely ∠ABD = ∠DBC. Therefore ∠ABC = 2∠ABD = 2 × 35° = 70°.
